A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAIGen. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy experiments, diffusion-model evaluations, attribute-amplification experiments and a 25-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds clustering comparisons, encoder robustness, interpretability generalization, sample-budget experiments and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The MSAE decomposition, minority-score equations, redundancy filtering and prompt-revision procedure remain unchanged. Label-free terminology clarifies the existing CLIP dependence; SigLIP is an ablation. The pooled-prompt footnote elaborates an extension already anticipated through shared-SAE training in v1's future work.

E1.justification: Both versions cover hierarchical toy data, WinoBias occupations and COCO scenes. Added promptwise analyses remain within these domains and tasks. FLUX.1-schnell was already evaluated in v1 Appendix F.2; its appearance in v2 Section 5.5 is a relocation.

E2.justification: V2 adds a direct image-level discovery comparator, CLIP k-means, across six professions (Table 6). It also evaluates Minority Guidance against base SDXL using a RAIGen-discovered attribute (Table 5), expanding comparison with statistical rarity sampling. This latter experiment is not a direct RAIGen amplification contest. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce k-means with 50 clusters and selection of the ten smallest, a controlled CLIP/SigLIP substitution, and sample budgets of 100, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000. Existing main protocols remain unchanged. The annotation-prompt attribution changes from Llama 4-Scout to GPT-5.2, resolving inconsistent documentation without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds encoder robustness, interpretability analysis across nine further prompt settings, sample-complexity and computational-cost studies, and analyses contrasting discovery with clustering and rarity sampling. These substantially broaden validation beyond v1's retained SAE, coarse-level-size and score-component ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 seeds for the toy experiment and 95% confidence intervals for the user study. The added appendix experiments do not introduce new repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results: animal presence of 0.150 under base SDXL versus 0.382 with Minority Guidance; six clustering comparisons, including doctor presence of 0.30 versus RAIGen's 0.15; 9/10 neuron agreement across encoders; and promptwise, sample-budget and runtime results. Original benchmark, user-study, amplification and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, the SAE/MSAE formulations and Equations 1–4 are retained. The added sample-complexity section is empirical and introduces no theoretical bound, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace unsupervised discovery and independence from external language models with the narrower claim of label-free discovery requiring no predefined minority categories. The main claims about rare-attribute discovery, cross-architecture auditing and amplification remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix B distinguishes discovering rare attributes from deciding whether they warrant intervention and develops RAIGen's upstream diagnostic role. Added analyses explain clustering shortcomings, encoder agreement, small-sample failure and computational cost. Section 4.2 explicitly acknowledges the pretrained semantic prior; the original limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link, comparator implementation settings and a runtime breakdown on one NVIDIA A100 with 40 GB memory, reporting approximately 72 minutes per prompt. It also corrects the annotation-model attribution. Existing training hyperparameters and annotation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning relative to Minority Guidance, Rare-to-Frequent and ToRA, presenting discovery as complementary to rare generation. It adds discussion of DiffLens and RespoDiff and connects suppression findings to Whac-A-Mole and SEBRA. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted language corrections, updates affiliations and publication text, adds acknowledgements, separates Discussion from Future work, and moves the FLUX subsection into the main text. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds compact appendix tables for the new comparisons and analyses and relocates the FLUX figure from Figure 7 to Figure 5. Existing figures retain their content, with limited resizing, table relocation and page reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through a direct clustering baseline, robustness and sample-budget studies, and runtime disclosure, while qualifying the label-free claim. Reporting errors temper these gains: Table 6's CLIP rows average approximately 0.438, not 0.37, and only four settings in Tables 9–10 exceed 0.80 interpretability, not the stated seven. These inconsistencies weaken the new summaries without reversing the comparative trends, supporting a limited net improvement.
